engineManufacturers.name: BMW M12/13
engineManufacturers.desc: The benchmark hybrid architecture. Exceptional ERS and top-end power.

engineManufacturers.name: Ferrari Tipo 032
engineManufacturers.desc: Raw power leader. Slightly less refined ERS than the silver works engine but devastating on power tracks.

engineManufacturers.name: Honda RA166E
engineManufacturers.desc: Exclusive works deal with the British racing-green outfit. Strong hybrid efficiency and compact packaging.

engineManufacturers.name: Ford GBA V6
engineManufacturers.desc: A new works powertrain programme with external manufacturer support. High-upside engine for Milton Keynes Racing and Toro GP.

engineManufacturers.name: TAG-Porsche TTE P01
engineManufacturers.desc: New entrant. Behind now but aggressive development trajectory — could be a dark horse by 2029.

engineManufacturers.name: Renault EF15B
engineManufacturers.desc: New 1986 engines built by Renault. Lotus and Ligier have the most updated version as the Renault factory team left F1.

engineManufacturers.name: BMW M12/13/1
engineManufacturers.desc: Tilted engine built for exclusive use of Brabham.

engineManufacturers.name: Motori Moderni 615-90
engineManufacturers.desc: Recent entrants to Formula One. Minardi has the exclusive supply of these engines,

engineManufacturers.name: Alfa Romeo 890T
engineManufacturers.desc: Alfa Romeo very old and unreliable engines. Only used by Osella.

engineManufacturers.name: Renault EF4B
engineManufacturers.desc: This is the 1985 engine of Renault, used by Tyrrell

td.name: Patrick Head
td.desc: The engineering backbone of Williams who famously designed the ultra-robust, championship-winning FW11 chassis.

td.name: John Barnard
td.desc: A design visionary who revolutionized Formula 1 by pioneering carbon-fiber monocoques and tight rear car packaging.

td.name: Gordon Murray
td.desc: A radical design genius who pushed physics to the limit in 1986 with the experimental, ultra-low-line BT55.

td.name: Gérard Ducarouge
td.desc: An elegant French designer whose lightweight aerodynamic concepts formed a lethal combination with Ayrton Senna's raw speed.

td.name: Harvey Postlethwaite
td.desc: A highly respected British engineer tasked with taming Ferrari's brutal turbo engine power with improved chassis handling.

td.name: Rory Byrne
td.desc: A highly creative aerodynamicist whose striking B186 chassis gave the team its spectacular maiden victory in Mexico.

td.name: Neil Oatley
td.desc: A thoroughly meticulous designer who crafted a highly polished, clean chassis for this ambitious, short-lived American entry.

td.name: Michel Tétu
td.desc: A practical French engineer who cleverly optimized the proven Renault turbo package to score consistent podiums early in the year.

td.name: Maurice Philippe
td.desc: A veteran designer who worked miracles on a limited budget to transition Tyrrell safely into the high-horsepower turbo era.

td.name: Dave Wass
td.desc: A pragmatic designer who prioritized mechanical durability to keep his drivers competitive within a brutal midfield.

td.name: Paul Brown
td.desc: An ambitious engineer who undertook the immense task of developing both the chassis and the proprietary engine for Germany's sole entry.

td.name: Giacomo Caliri
td.desc: An experienced Italian aerodynamicist who worked tirelessly to lay a functional engineering foundation for the young Faenza squad.

td.name: Giuseppe Petrotta
td.desc: A resilient technical director who performed minor miracles to keep a highly underfunded package running on the grid.

rs.name: Ron Dennis
rs.desc: A relentless perfectionist whose masterful tactical planning and fuel calculation calls secured Alain Prost the 1986 championship.

rs.name: Peter Windsor
rs.desc: Managed trackside operations during a turbulent year, carefully handling the explosive rivalry between Mansell and Piquet.

rs.name: Peter Warr
rs.desc: A sharp-witted operator who built the team's entire operational and political focus around the brilliance of Ayrton Senna.

rs.name: Ken Tyrrell
rs.desc: The legendary team boss who leveraged decades of elite tactical intuition to out-maneuver better-funded factory teams.

rs.name: Herbie Blash
rs.desc: A highly adaptable team manager who held the crew together and made calm tactical decisions through a very difficult transition year.

rs.name: Marco Piccinini
rs.desc: A commanding tactical figure who used his deep political savvy to keep Ferrari afloat during a mechanically grueling campaign.

rs.name: Peter Collins
rs.desc: A clever strategist who orchestrated a brilliant tire-management plan that completely outsmarted the grid at the Mexican Grand Prix.

rs.name: Teddy Mayer
rs.desc: A veteran executive who brought immense championship-winning poise to guide this new team's operational strategy from the pit wall.

rs.name: Guy Ligier
rs.desc: A fiercely passionate team owner whose emotional, aggressive race calls extracted everything possible from his French machinery.

rs.name: Jackie Oliver
rs.desc: A shrewd, realistic operator who constructed risk-averse strategies designed to capitalize on the mechanical failures of faster cars.

rs.name: Giancarlo Minardi
rs.desc: A deeply beloved figure whose tactical gambles aimed to give his raw, young drivers the best shot at seeing the checkered flag.

rs.name: Erich Zakowski
rs.desc: A dedicated team owner who micro-managed his pit wall to focus strictly on maximizing reliability and learning for his home-grown squad.

rs.name: Enzo Osella
rs.desc: A courageous underdog who focused his minimal resources on making the grid and surviving the brutal mechanical attrition of the era.

cm.name: Joan Villadelprat
cm.desc: A world-class wrench who ensured Alain Prost’s McLaren cars were built with absolute mechanical perfection and surgical precision.

cm.name: Alan Challis
cm.desc: Ran a highly disciplined garage capable of maintaining the complex Honda turbos at a flawless performance standard all year.

cm.name: Charlie Whiting
cm.desc: A brilliant mechanical mind whose leadership in the Brabham garage ensured the radical, lay-down BMW engines were expertly installed.

cm.name: Nigel Stepney
cm.desc: Ayrton Senna’s preferred mechanic whose intense work ethic kept the fragile Renault-powered Lotus operating at peak qualifying trim.

cm.name: Valerio Riva
cm.desc: A passionate leader who held Maranello’s crew together under high pressure despite frequent, heartbreaking engine failures.

cm.name: John Walton
cm.desc: Brought immense grit from the old Toleman squad to mold Benetton's fresh garage into a highly professional, race-winning unit.

cm.name: Mick Cook
cm.desc: Maintained exceptional build quality on the brand-new Ford-powered cars, earning widespread respect across the paddock for his efficiency.

cm.name: Jean-Pierre Diot
cm.desc: A loyal veteran who knew the ins and outs of French motorsport, ensuring the Ligier chassis was robust and well-prepared.

cm.name: Roger Hill
cm.desc: An old-school mechanic who kept the Tyrrell garage organized and highly efficient despite working with a tiny workforce.

cm.name: Greg Baker
cm.desc: A reliable midfield veteran who specialized in quick, structural repairs to ensure maximum running time during practice and qualifying.

cm.name: Helmut Barth
cm.desc: A tireless technician who meticulously managed the unique demands of Zakspeed’s highly volatile, custom in-house turbo engine.

cm.name: Paolo Dalla Rosa
cm.desc: Directed a young, passionate crew of mechanics who worked late into the night to overcome the teething issues of a new chassis.

cm.name: Felice Noe
cm.desc: A true survivor of the pit lane who masterfully fabricated parts out of nothing to ensure his cars simply made the race.

pcc.name: Neil Trundle
pcc.desc: Ron Dennis’s trusted right-hand man who brought a legendary standard of synchronization and calm to the high-stakes McLaren pit stops.

pcc.name: Bob McMurray
pcc.desc: Drilled the Williams crew to execute lightning-fast tire swaps that proved critical during the tight championship battles.

pcc.name: Bob Dance
pcc.desc: A revered Lotus icon whose steady composure calmed the crew during high-pressure stops for a charging Ayrton Senna.

pcc.name: David Sims
pcc.desc: A legendary figure who ran flawless pit lanes back when Brabham was pioneering the art of the modern tactical fuel stop.

pcc.name: Pietro Corradini
pcc.desc: Infused the Scuderia pit crew with immense Italian passion, demanding rapid, coordinated physical execution under immense media scrutiny.

pcc.name: Steve Matchett
pcc.desc: A sharp, fast-learning technician who brought a modern, analytical approach to crew execution on the pit lane.

pcc.name: Daniel Champion
pcc.desc: Kept the French crew perfectly focused and disciplined during chaotic, rain-threatened pit stops throughout the 1986 season.

pcc.name: Frank Coppuck
pcc.desc: Implemented slick, American-inspired drill routines to ensure the new team's pit stops were competitive from day one.

pcc.name: Simon Morley
pcc.desc: Compensated for a lack of automated equipment with highly coordinated, muscle-memory teamwork that punched well above its weight.

pcc.name: James Robinson
pcc.desc: Focused heavily on safe, error-free wheel changes to avoid throwing away hard-earned midfield positions.

pcc.name: Heinz-Jürgen Schorle
pcc.desc: Led a small but incredibly patriotic German crew that took immense pride in clean, steady pit lane execution.

pcc.name: Bruno Garagnani
pcc.desc: Managed a volatile but enthusiastic group, prioritizing structural safety and clear communication over raw speed.

pcc.name: Stefano Osella
pcc.desc: Bravely directed a skeleton crew under immense stress, ensuring that basic tire swaps were completed safely on a shoestring budget.
